nodes.text: M-morning. Or whatever it is by now. The pond keeps its own clock.

choices.text: Where does the water go, downriver?
Why ring the bell at dawn?

nodes.text: Down to *Saltmere*. In the end. Salt flats, grey gulls, boats with eyes painted on them. I walked up from there, when I was small. One day I'll pole somebody the whole way back down. When I've got the nerve.
So the pond knows I'm here. And so *Garton* knows. He'd never ask. But his window faces the water, and the bell saves him the walk. The wind rings it sometimes, on its own. I let it.
Trout, mostly. The pond's generous if you're p-patient. Rod's for sale too, if you'd rather catch your own.
You too. Mind the reeds if you swim. They *are* clingy.
